request.spec:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every successful change to a sheet now writes one line to the audit file, and all 4 tests pass when I run `bin/e2e`.

**How it works**
- **Who made the change:** until now the server never received the signed-in user's name. The front end (`PersonForm.tsx` and `PersonClaims.tsx`) now adds it as a `?user=<name>` parameter on the four save requests (add or edit a person, add or edit a claim).
- **Writing the line:** each of those four endpoints has a new audit step between saving and responding. The steps are `AuditPersonAdded`, `AuditPersonEdited`, `AuditClaimAdded` and `AuditClaimEdited`, and each writes its line through the app's existing audit service:
  - `PERSON_ADDED` / `PERSON_EDITED sheet=… by=… name=… grade=…`
  - `CLAIM_ADDED` / `CLAIM_EDITED sheet=… by=… person=… amount=… date=…`, with amounts to two decimals and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. An edited claim looks up its person's current name.
- **Refusals:** any rule that refuses a change, now or added later, stops the request before the audit step runs. So a refused change writes no line and nothing to the store.

**Things to know**
- An edit is logged whenever it saves, even if nothing actually changed.
- The audit line is written just before the database commits. If a commit failed after that, the file would show a change the store doesn't have; nothing in the current setup should make that happen.
- The `user` parameter is required: a save request sent without it fails, which would affect any other client calling these endpoints. The app's own screens always send it.
